proposals: The Ministry of Power should publish the approved CCUS Mission scheme document, with its outlay, capture-capacity target, funding structure and R&D fund, so the ₹19,700 crore, 7 million-tonne and ₹2,500 crore figures now known only from trade press can be confirmed or corrected.

The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change should publish an updated technology-readiness assessment of CCUS alongside its long-term strategy, explaining what changed after the 2022 LT-LEDS judged it fit only for demonstration projects, so the ₹20,000 crore commitment rests on a stated public rationale.

NITI Aayog should release the year-by-year data tables behind all eleven scenario volumes, including coal consumption, sectoral energy use and emissions, in downloadable form, so the finding that coal use rises until 2047 can be checked against the model rather than press releases.

NITI Aayog should publish a with-CCUS and without-CCUS sensitivity run of its Industry and Power scenarios, so the contribution of capture to the roughly one-quarter of industrial energy expected to stay fossil-based in 2070 is quantified officially.

The Department of Science and Technology, with the Geological Survey of India, should publish an official basin-by-basin estimate of CO₂ geological storage capacity, so policy does not rest on an academic range of 400 to 600-plus gigatonnes that no government source has stated.
